# BlitzBasic: Math

Trigonometry, rounding, random numbers and other numeric helpers.


Back to [[BlitzBasic]] or the [[Command-Index]].

| Command | Returns | Summary |
|---|---|---|
| [ACos](BlitzBasic-Math#acos) | Float | Returns the angle whose cosine is the given number. |
| [ASin](BlitzBasic-Math#asin) | Float | Returns the angle whose sine is the given number. |
| [ATan](BlitzBasic-Math#atan) | Float | Returns the angle whose tangent is the given number, in degrees from -90 to 90. |
| [ATan2](BlitzBasic-Math#atan2) | Float | Returns the angle of the point (`b`, `a`) seen from the origin, in degrees from -180 to 180. |
| [Ceil](BlitzBasic-Math#ceil) | Float | Rounds up to the next whole number and returns it as a float. |
| [Cos](BlitzBasic-Math#cos) | Float | Returns the cosine of an angle given in degrees, not radians. |
| [Exp](BlitzBasic-Math#exp) | Float | Returns e (2.71828...) raised to the given power. |
| [Floor](BlitzBasic-Math#floor) | Float | Rounds down to the previous whole number and returns it as a float. |
| [Log](BlitzBasic-Math#log) | Float | Returns the natural logarithm (base e) of a number. |
| [Log10](BlitzBasic-Math#log10) | Float | Returns the logarithm to base 10, which is how many times 10 goes into the number. |
| [Rand](BlitzBasic-Math#rand) | Int | Returns a random whole number from `from` to `to`, both included. |
| [Rnd](BlitzBasic-Math#rnd) | Float | Returns a random float from `from` up to, but not including, `to`. |
| [RndSeed](BlitzBasic-Math#rndseed) | Int |  |
| [SeedRnd](BlitzBasic-Math#seedrnd) | None | Restarts the random number generator from a seed. |
| [Sin](BlitzBasic-Math#sin) | Float | Returns the sine of an angle given in degrees, not radians. |
| [Sqr](BlitzBasic-Math#sqr) | Float | Returns the square root of a number. |
| [Tan](BlitzBasic-Math#tan) | Float | Returns the tangent of an angle given in degrees, not radians. |

### ACos

```blitzbasic
ACos float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns the angle whose cosine is the given number. The result is in degrees, from 0 to 180. A number outside -1 to 1 has no such angle.

```blitzbasic
Print ACos(0.5)
```

```text
60.0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | The cosine, from -1 to 1. |

**Returns:** The angle in degrees.

### ASin

```blitzbasic
ASin float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns the angle whose sine is the given number. The result is in degrees, from -90 to 90.

```blitzbasic
Print ASin(0.5)
```

```text
30.0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | The sine, from -1 to 1. |

**Returns:** The angle in degrees.

### ATan

```blitzbasic
ATan float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns the angle whose tangent is the given number, in degrees from -90 to 90. When you have both sides of the triangle, [ATan2](BlitzBasic-Math#atan2) is usually the better choice because it knows which quadrant the angle is in.

```blitzbasic
Print ATan(1)
```

```text
45.0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | The tangent. |

**Returns:** The angle in degrees.

### ATan2

```blitzbasic
ATan2 floata#, floatb#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns the angle of the point (`b`, `a`) seen from the origin, in degrees from -180 to 180. Note the order: the vertical distance `a` comes first. 0 points along positive x, 90 along positive y.

```blitzbasic
Print ATan2(1, 1)
Print ATan2(0, -1)
```

```text
45.0
180.0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `floata` | Float | required | The vertical distance (y). |
| `floatb` | Float | required | The horizontal distance (x). |

**Returns:** The angle in degrees.

### Ceil

```blitzbasic
Ceil float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Rounds up to the next whole number and returns it as a float.

```blitzbasic
Print Ceil(2.1)
Print Ceil(-2.1)
```

```text
3.0
-2.0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | The number to round up. |

**Returns:** The smallest whole number that is not below `float`.

### Cos

```blitzbasic
Cos degrees#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns the cosine of an angle given in degrees, not radians.

```blitzbasic
Print Cos(60)
```

```text

```

|---|---|---|---|

### Exp

```blitzbasic
Exp float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns e (2.71828...) raised to the given power. It is the opposite of [Log](BlitzBasic-Math#log).

```blitzbasic
Print Exp(1)
```

```text
2.71828
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | The exponent. |

**Returns:** e to the power of `float`.

### Floor

```blitzbasic
Floor float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Rounds down to the previous whole number and returns it as a float.

```blitzbasic
Print Floor(2.9)
Print Floor(-2.1)
```

```text

-3.0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | The number to round down. |

### Log

```blitzbasic
Log float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns the natural logarithm (base e) of a number. For base 10 use [Log10](BlitzBasic-Math#log10).

```blitzbasic
Print Log(10)
```

```text
2.30259
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | A number above 0. |

**Returns:** The natural logarithm.

### Log10

```blitzbasic
Log10 float#  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns the logarithm to base 10, which is how many times 10 goes into the number.

```blitzbasic
Print Log10(1000)
```

```text
3.0
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `float` | Float | required | A number above 0. |

**Returns:** The logarithm to base 10.

### Rand

```blitzbasic
Rand from%, to%=1  ; returns Int
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns a random whole number from `from` to `to`, both included. With one argument the range is 1 up to that number. The same seed (see [SeedRnd](BlitzBasic-Math#seedrnd)) always gives the same sequence.

```blitzbasic
SeedRnd 1234
dice = Rand(1, 6)
Print dice >= 1 And dice <= 6
Print Rand(5, 5)
```

```text
1
5
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | Int | required | Lowest result, or the highest when `to` is left out. |
| `to` | Int | `1` | Highest result. Defaults to 1. |

**Returns:** A random integer in the range.

### Rnd

```blitzbasic
Rnd from#, to#=0  ; returns Float
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Returns a random float from `from` up to, but not including, `to`. With one argument the range is 0 up to that number.

```blitzbasic
SeedRnd 7
r# = Rnd(5, 6)
Print r >= 5 And r < 6
```

```text
1
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | Float | required | Lowest result, or the limit when `to` is left out. |
| `to` | Float | `0` | The limit, never reached. Defaults to 0. |

**Returns:** A random float in the range.

### RndSeed

```blitzbasic
RndSeed  ; returns Int
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

_Not documented yet._

**Returns:** The current seed of the random number generator. Store it and give it to [SeedRnd](BlitzBasic-Math#seedrnd) later to replay a sequence of random numbers.

### SeedRnd

```blitzbasic
SeedRnd seed%
```

**Works in:** Blitz2D, BlitzPlus, Blitz3D

Restarts the random number generator from a seed. The same seed always gives the same numbers from [Rand](BlitzBasic-Math#rand) and [Rnd](BlitzBasic-Math#rnd), which is useful for replays and procedurally generated levels. Every program starts with the same seed (4660), so it gets the same random numbers on every run until you use `SeedRnd MilliSecs()` for different ones.

```blitzbasic
SeedRnd 42
a = Rand(1, 1000)
SeedRnd 42
b = Rand(1, 1000)
Print a = b
```

```text
1
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `seed` | Int | required | The starting value. |
